chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The diyah for accidental killing, when the man did not intend the killing, is one hundred camels, or ten thousand of silver coins, or one thousand sheep."

And he said: "The aggravated diyah, which resembles intentional killing but is not intentional, is weightier than the diyah of accidental killing in the ages of the camels: thirty-three ḥiqqahs, thirty-three jadhaʿahs, and thirty-four thaniyyahs, all of them covered by a stud camel."

And I asked him about the diyah, so he said: "The diyah of a Muslim is ten thousand of silver, or one thousand mithqals of gold, or one thousand sheep according to their ages in three divisions, and of camels one hundred, for they are according to their ages, and of cattle two hundred."

key_terms.الشَّاةِ: sheep, one of the accepted forms of diyah payment
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, one of the standard forms of diyah payment
key_terms.الْبَقَرِ: cattle, another accepted form of diyah payment
key_terms.الْمُغَلَّظَةِ: the aggravated or intensified form of diyah
key_terms.الْوَرِقِ: silver currency used as a measure of compensation
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْخَطَإِ: the financial compensation due for accidental killing

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for accidental killing and شبه العمد in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal rulings for diyah in cases of accidental killing and the aggravated form that resembles intentional killing without being fully intentional. It specifies the accepted forms and quantities of compensation, including camels, silver, gold, sheep, and cattle, and distinguishes the more severe category by the prescribed ages of the camels.
